title: progressive-sweepbench-and-compact-heatline-serializer
text:
progressive-sweepbench-and-compact-heatline-serializer

description:
Motivation: We need a compact, repeatable way to sweep throughput and batch-size configurations while preserving kernel-level signal for short (2–5s) microbench runs. Existing sweep runners produce bulky trace bundles that are slow to upload and hard to diff. This PR introduces a progressive sweepbench runner that performs stepped load ramps and a compact 'heatline' serializer that compresses per-window latency histograms and kernel-sample signatures into a small, diff-friendly artifact.

What this PR adds: 1) bench/sweep/progressive_sweepbench.py — orchestrates stepwise QPS/batch sweeps with adaptive dwell times (auto-extend for noisy tails). 2) bench/reporters/heatline_serializer.py — emits compact TSV/JSONL heatline artifacts (time window, qps, batch_size, p50/p95/p99, microkernel-hash). 3) bench/profiles/kernel_sampler.c — lightweight JNI/extension that samples GPU kernel events for 1–2ms windows and summarizes hot kernels into a stable 64-bit fingerprint. 4) docs/benchmark/sweep_playbook.md — guidance for reproducing runs and interpreting heatlines. 5) CI integration: add a smoke bench job that validates serializer output schema.

Design notes: - Progressive sweeps: rather than fixed-duration steps, the runner watches for quantile convergence and extends the dwell when p99 variance exceeds threshold. This reduces noisy measurements and produces more reliable trendlines. - Heatline format: each line encodes a window with fields [timestamp, qps, batch_size, p50, p95, p99, kernel_fingerprint, sample_count, cpu_rps]. The kernel_fingerprint is a stable hex digest derived from sorted kernel name+duration buckets; it's intentionally low-entropy to keep artifacts small while being useful for correlating hotpaths. - Compactness: the serializer supports gzip and an experimental delta-encoding mode that emits only changed lines relative to a baseline run.

Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests for serializer (schema, delta mode, roundtrip) included. - Local runs on a 4xA100 node comparing standard profiler bundles vs heatline artifacts showed >10x size reduction (avg 2.8MB vs 35MB) with preserved top-3 kernel fingerprints for each window. - Two staged CI runs: initial smoke job failed on first iteration because the kernel sampler needed a higher ulimit; fixed in commit 3.

Safety and rollout: non-breaking. Feature gated behind BENCH_HEATLINE env flag. Default behavior unchanged until flag enabled.

How to use (short): 
$ BENCH_HEATLINE=1 python -m bench.sweep.progressive_sweepbench --model gpt-j-6b --qps-start 5 --qps-end 200 --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8 --out ./runs/sweep01

Next steps / follow-ups: - Add automatic baseline diffing in the benchmark dashboard. - Wire heatline uploader to benchstore with lineage metadata.

Related: ENG-3245 (benchmark stability), ENG-3298 (kernel fingerprinting prototype).

review_conversation:
Liam Chen: Can we avoid sampling kernel names on every window? The initial runs showed a small CPU spike.
Ava Patel: We sample at 1–2ms per-window and aggregate; CPU overhead is ~1–2%. I've added README notes and the sampler uses eBPF filter + adaptive duty cycle.
Sofia Ramirez: Need clearer guidance on when to extend dwell. "We should avoid overextending for noisy GPUs."
Ava Patel: Added CLI flags --max-extend-seconds and --variance-threshold and defaults tuned from lab runs.
Noah Green: Approved after the ulimit fix and smaller test matrix in CI.


ci_checks:
bench-smoke (ubuntu-latest) — passed after rerun; lint — passed; unit-tests — passed; integration bench-lite — passed (flaky on first run, addressed by commit e6fa1bb). CI artifacts include sample heatline outputs under actions/artifacts for quick inspection.

release_notes:
Added a progressive sweepbench runner and compact 'heatline' serializer for small, diff-friendly benchmark artifacts. Gate behind BENCH_HEATLINE. Improves portability and upload performance of microbench traces.

notes_for_qa:
QA should run a short sweep (qps 5->50) with BENCH_HEATLINE=1 and compare kernel_fingerprint stability across two repeats. If fingerprints diverge significantly, re-run with --max-extend-seconds 60 to reduce noise.

additional_context:
This PR is intended to complement larger profiling exporters already in benchlab. It focuses on fast iteration and small artifacts for CI and triage. Follow-on work will integrate with benchstore lineage and dashboard diffing.
